Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 57, verses 1–6:

It is Madaniyya (revealed in Medina).

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} He, the Exalted, informs of His greatness, His majesty, and the vastness of His dominion: that all that is in the heavens and the earth, of the speaking creatures [and the silent ones] and others, and the inanimate things, glorify their Lord and declare Him far above what does not befit His majesty; that they are obedient to their Lord and submissive to His might, and that the traces of His wisdom are manifest in them. For this reason He said: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾. This contains a clarification of the universal need of the created beings, the higher and the lower, for their Lord in all their conditions, the universality of His might and dominance over all things, and the universality of His wisdom in His creation and His command.

{2} Then He informs of the universality of His sovereignty, saying: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death﴾; that is, He is the Creator of that, the Provider, the One who manages it by His power. ﴿And He is over all things competent﴾.

{3} ﴿He is the First﴾: the One before whom there is nothing. ﴿And the Last﴾: the One after whom there is nothing. ﴿And the Apparent﴾: the One above whom there is nothing. ﴿And the Hidden﴾: the One beneath whom there is nothing. ﴿And He is, of all things, Knowing﴾: His knowledge encompasses the apparent and the hidden, the secrets and the concealed, and the matters past and future.

{4} ﴿He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾: the first of them is Sunday, and the last of them is Friday. ﴿Then He istawa (rose) above the Throne﴾: an istiwa' befitting His majesty, above all His creation. ﴿He knows what enters into the earth﴾: of seeds, creatures, rain, and other things. ﴿And what emerges from it﴾: of plants, trees, creatures, and other things. ﴿And what descends from the heaven﴾: of angels, decrees, and provisions. ﴿And what ascends into it﴾: of angels, souls, supplications, deeds, and other things. ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾; like His saying: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth, nor fewer than that nor more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾. This companionship is the companionship of knowledge and observation. For this reason He warns and promises recompense for deeds, saying: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾; that is, He, the Exalted, sees what proceeds from you of deeds, and what those deeds proceed from of righteousness or wickedness. So He will recompense you for them and preserve them for you.

{5} ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾: in ownership, creation, and servitude, He disposes of them as He wills by His commands, both decreed and legislated, which proceed according to divine wisdom. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾: of deeds and doers, so that the servants are presented before Him, the wicked is distinguished from the good, and He recompenses the doer of good for his goodness and the doer of evil for his evil.

{6} ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾; that is, He makes the night enter upon the day, so that night covers them with its darkness, and they rest and become still. Then He makes the day enter upon the night, so that the darkness upon the earth departs, the universe becomes bright, the servants move, and they go forth to their interests and livelihoods. Allah continues to wind the night over the day and the day over the night, and alternates between them in increase and decrease, length and shortness, until by this the seasons are established, the times are regulated, and the benefits that are attained thereby are attained. ﴿So blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, and exalted is the Generous, the Bountiful, who has bestowed upon His servants the apparent and hidden blessings. ﴿And He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾; that is, of what occurs in the breasts of the worlds, so He grants success to whoever He knows is worthy of it, and forsakes whoever He knows is not fit for His guidance.

{8} Then He mentioned the cause that calls them to belief and the absence of any hindrance to it, saying: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not believe in God, while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are [truly] believers?﴾; that is, what prevents you from belief when the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), the best of the messengers and the most noble caller who has ever called to God, is calling you? This is something that requires haste in responding to his call, answering, and accepting the truth he has brought. And He has already taken from you the pledge and covenant of belief, if you are believers.

{9} Moreover, out of His kindness and care for you, He did not suffice with merely the call of the Messenger, who is the noblest of the world; rather He strengthened him with miracles and guided you to the truth of what he brought by clear signs. Therefore He said: ﴿It is He who sends down to His servant clear signs﴾; that is, manifest signs that show people of understanding the soundness of everything he brought, and that it is the certain truth. ﴿That He may bring you out﴾ — through the sending of the Messenger to you and what God sent down through him of the Book and wisdom — ﴿from darknesses into light﴾; that is, from the darknesses of ignorance and disbelief into the light of knowledge and faith. This is from His mercy and compassion toward you, for He is more merciful to His servants than a mother to her child. ﴿And indeed, God is to you Kind and Merciful.﴾

{10} ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the way of God, when to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth?﴾; that is, what prevents you from spending in the cause of God, which comprises all paths of goodness, and what makes you stingy, [when] you have nothing, but rather ﴿to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾: all wealth will pass out of your hands, or you will pass away from it, and then ownership returns to its owner, may He be blessed and exalted. So seize the opportunity to spend while the wealth is in your hands, and seize the chance. Then He, may He be exalted, mentioned the differing merits of deeds according to circumstances and divine wisdom, saying: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards.﴾ The conquest intended here is the conquest of Hudaybiyyah, when the truce took place between the Messenger and Quraysh, which is among the greatest conquests, in which the spreading of Islam occurred, Muslims mixed with disbelievers, and the call to the religion took place without opposition. From that time people entered the religion of God in multitudes, and Islam became greatly honoured. Before this conquest, Muslims could not call to the religion except in the region whose people had embraced it, such as Madinah and its surroundings, and whoever embraced Islam from the people of Makkah and other abodes of the polytheists was harmed and feared. Therefore, whoever embraced Islam before the conquest [and spent] and fought had greater rank, reward and recompense than those who did not embrace Islam, fight, and spend until after that, as the requirement of wisdom demands. For this reason, the foremost and most excellent of the Companions were mostly those who embraced Islam before the conquest. Since preference among matters may give rise to the suspicion of deficiency and disparagement of the one less preferred, God guarded against this by saying: ﴿And to each God has promised the best﴾; that is, those who embraced Islam, fought and spent before the conquest and after it, all of them, God promised them Paradise. This indicates the virtue of all the Companions, may God be pleased with them, since God bore witness to their belief and promised them Paradise. ﴿And God is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ He will recompense each of you for what He knows of his deed.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 57, verse 18–19:

{18} ﴿Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity﴾: with the letters doubled (al-mutassadiqin); that is, those who give abundantly in lawful charity (sadaqat shar'iyyah) and pleasing expenditures (nafaqat mardiyyah). ﴿And who have loaned Allah a goodly loan﴾: by putting forward from their wealth, in the paths of good, that which will be a store for them with their Lord. ﴿It will be multiplied for them﴾: the good deed will be multiplied tenfold, up to seven hundred times, and up to many times over. ﴿And they will have a noble reward﴾: which is what Allah has prepared for them in Paradise, which no soul knows.

{19} ﴿And those who believed in Allah and His messengers﴾: Faith (iman), according to the people of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah), is what the Book and the Sunnah indicate: it is the saying of the heart and tongue, and the action of the heart, tongue and limbs. This includes all the apparent and hidden laws of the religion. Those who combined [between] these matters ﴿are the siddiqun (the truthful ones)﴾; that is, those whose rank is above the rank of the believers in general and below the rank of the prophets. As for His saying: ﴿And the martyrs, with their Lord, they will have their reward and their light﴾; as has been related in the sound hadith: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred degrees, the distance between each two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His cause." This indicates the great height of their station, their elevation, and their nearness to Allah, the Exalted. ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾.

These verses gather the categories of creation: the charitable (al-mutasaddiqin), the truthful (al-siddiqun), the martyrs, and the companions of the Blazing Fire. The charitable are those whose greatest deeds are kindness to creation and bestowing benefit upon them to the utmost of their ability, especially benefit through wealth in the way of Allah. The truthful (al-siddiqun) are those who perfected the levels of faith, righteous action, beneficial knowledge and sincere certainty. The martyrs are those who fought in the way of Allah to elevate the word of Allah, giving up their souls and wealth, and were killed. The companions of the Blazing Fire are the disbelievers who denied the signs of Allah. There remains a category which Allah mentioned in Surah Fatir: the moderate (al-muqtasidun), who performed the obligations and abstained from the prohibitions, except that some of them fell short regarding the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants. Their final destination is Paradise, though some of them may receive punishment for some of what they did.

{20} Allah, may He be exalted, informs us of the reality of this worldly life and what it is like, and He makes clear its end and the end of its people: that it is {play and amusement}. Bodies play with it and hearts are diverted by it. What confirms this is what exists and takes place among the people of this world. You find them having spent the times of their lives in the amusement of their hearts and in heedlessness of the remembrance of Allah and of what lies before them of promise and threat. You see them having taken their religion as play and amusement. This is in contrast to the people of wakefulness and the workers for the Hereafter, whose hearts are filled with the remembrance of Allah, His knowledge and His love, and who have occupied their times with deeds that bring them closer to Allah, both those whose benefit is limited to themselves and those whose benefit extends to others. As for His words {and adornment}: that is, adornment in clothing, food, drink, mounts, houses, palaces, status and other things. {And boasting among yourselves}: that is, each one of its people wants to boast over the other and to be the dominant one in its affairs and the one who has fame in its circumstances. {And rivalry in wealth and children}: that is, each one wants to be the one who outnumbers others in wealth and children. This is confirmed by its occurrence among the lovers of this world and those who are content with it. This is in contrast to the one who knows the world and its reality, and so has made it a passageway and not a place of residence. He competes for what brings him closer to Allah, and adopts the means that lead him to the abode of His honour. And when he sees someone who outnumbers him and competes with him in wealth and children, he competes with him through righteous deeds.

Then Allah sets forth for this world a parable: rain that falls upon the earth, so that the plants of the earth become intermingled with it, of what people and livestock eat, until, when the earth takes on its adornment and its vegetation pleases the disbelievers who have limited their sight and their aspirations to this world, there comes upon it a command from Allah that destroys it. It dries up and withers and returns to its former state, as though it had never flourished green there nor had a lovely sight been seen in it. Likewise is this world: while it is bright and blossoming for its owner, whatever he desires of its objectives is attained, and whatever he turns to of its affairs, he finds its doors open. Then the decree strikes, removing it from his hand and ending his control over it, or taking him away from it, so he departs empty-handed, taking from it nothing but a shroud. Woe to the one whose greatest wish is this world and whose labour and striving are for it.

As for working for the Hereafter, it is what benefits and is stored up for its doer, and accompanies the servant forever. For this reason Allah, may He be exalted, said: {And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from Allah and approval}. That is, the state of the Hereafter is free of neither of these two matters: either severe punishment in the Fire of Hell, with its shackles, chains and terrors, for the one whose goal and ultimate aim was this world, so that he dared against the disobedience of Allah, denied the signs of Allah, and disbelieved the blessings of Allah; or forgiveness from Allah for sins and the removal of punishments, and approval from Allah, which settles whomever He settles in the Abode of Approval, for the one who knew the world and strove for the Hereafter with its striving. All of this calls to renunciation of this world and eagerness for the Hereafter. For this reason He said: {And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion}. That is, it is nothing but enjoyment through which one takes pleasure, benefits, and relieves needs. Only people of weak intellects are deceived by it and find rest in it, those whom the Deceiver has deluded concerning Allah.

{21} Then He commanded racing toward the forgiveness of Allah, His approval and His Garden. This is achieved by striving through the means of forgiveness: sincere repentance, beneficial seeking of forgiveness, and distancing oneself from sins and their places. And racing toward the approval of Allah is achieved through righteous deeds, and by constant eagerness for what pleases Allah, such as excellence in worshipping the Creator and excellence toward creation in all forms of benefit. For this reason Allah mentioned the deeds that necessitate this, saying: {And a Garden whose width is like the width of heaven and earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers}. Belief in Allah and His messengers encompasses the fundamentals of religion and its branches. {That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills}: that is, this which We have made clear to you, and We have mentioned for you the paths leading to Paradise and the paths leading to the Fire, and that the reward of Allah with its great recompense and its beautiful reward is among the greatest of His favours and bounty upon His servants. {And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty}: whose praise cannot be counted, indeed He is as He has praised Himself, and beyond whatever any of His creatures could praise Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 57, verse 22–24:

{22} He, may He be exalted, says, informing about the comprehensiveness of His decree and His predestination: {No calamity befalls on the earth or in yourselves}. This includes all the calamities that afflict creation, whether good or evil; all of them have been written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), the small and the great alike. This is a tremendous matter that the minds cannot encompass, and before which the hearts of people of understanding (ulu al-albab) are bewildered. Yet it is easy for Allah.

{23} Allah informed His servants of this so that this principle would be firmly established in them, and they would build upon it what befalls them of good and evil. Thus they will not despair or grieve over what has escaped them of that which their souls longed for and aspired to, knowing that it is written in the Preserved Tablet and must certainly come to pass; there is no way to repel it. And they will not rejoice with the exultant joy of arrogance and insolence over what Allah has given them, knowing that they did not attain it by their own power and strength, but rather by Allah's bounty and favor. Instead, they will occupy themselves with thanking the One who bestows blessings and repels afflictions. Hence He said: {Indeed, Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful}; that is, the arrogant, harsh, coarse, self-admiring, and boastful one who attributes the blessings of Allah to himself, which makes him transgress and distracts him; as Allah, the Exalted, said: {And if We let him taste mercy from Us after hardship has touched him, he says, "This is mine due to [my] knowledge." Rather, it is a trial}.

{24} {Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon the people}; that is, they combine two blameworthy matters, each of which is sufficient for evil: stinginess, which is withholding obligatory rights, and enjoining people to do the same. Their own stinginess was not enough for them, until they commanded the people to do so and urged them [to adopt] this blameworthy trait by their words and deeds. This is among their turning away from obedience to their Lord and their turning their backs on it. {And whoever turns away}: from obedience to Allah, then he harms only himself, and he will never harm Allah in the least. {Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy}: whose self-sufficiency is inherent to His essence, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and who enriched His servants and gave them sufficiency. The Praiseworthy is the One to whom belongs every beautiful name, every perfect attribute, and every beautiful act, deserving to be praised, extolled, and magnified.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 57, verse 28–29:

{28} This address may be understood as addressed to the People of the Book who believed in Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus), peace be upon them both. He commands them to act in accordance with the requirements of their faith: by fearing Allah, abandoning His disobedience, and believing in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). And if they do that, Allah will give them ﴿a double portion of His mercy﴾; that is, two shares of reward: one share for their faith in the earlier Prophets, and one share for their faith in Muhammad (ﷺ). It may also be understood as a general command, encompassing the People of the Book and others, and this is the apparent meaning. Allah commanded them to have faith and taqwa (God-consciousness), which encompasses the entire religion, outward and inward, its roots and its branches. If they comply with this great command, Allah [will give them] ﴿a double portion of His mercy﴾, the true extent and description of which none knows except Allah the Exalted: a reward for faith and a reward for taqwa; or a reward for carrying out the commands and a reward for avoiding the prohibitions; or the dual form is meant to indicate that the giving is repeated, time after time. ﴿And He will make for you a light by which you will walk﴾; that is, He will give you knowledge, guidance and light by which you will walk through the darknesses of ignorance, and He will forgive you your sins. ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾: so the abundance of this reward should not be considered strange, given the bounty of the Possessor of great bounty, whose bounty has encompassed the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth; no creature is free of His bounty for the blink of an eye or less than that.

{29} And His saying: ﴿That the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾; that is, We have made clear to you Our bounty and Our kindness towards those who believe with a comprehensive faith, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; so that the People of the Scripture may have knowledge that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah; that is, they cannot restrict Allah according to their desires and their corrupt intellects, saying: ﴿None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian﴾, and wishing upon Allah corrupt wishes. So Allah the Exalted informed that those who believe in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and fear Allah have a double portion of His mercy, and light, and forgiveness, in spite of the noses of the People of the Scripture; ﴿and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾: to whom His wisdom, exalted is He, decrees that He should give of His bounty. ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾: whose extent cannot be measured.

[End of the commentary on Surat al-Hadid. To Allah belongs all praise and grace. All praise is due to Allah.]
